subject: chemistry
title: Diffusion and gas behaviour
key_idea: Gas particles move fast and randomly, and they hit the walls of their container to cause pressure. Heating a gas or lowering its pressure makes its volume bigger. **Diffusion** is the spreading of particles from high to low concentration, and gases with a lower relative molecular mass diffuse faster.

sections.heading: Temperature, pressure and the volume of a gas

blocks.text: A gas has no fixed shape or volume, so its volume changes with conditions. This section covers temperature and pressure, then explains them with particles.

items.meaning: The force of the particles hitting the walls of the container, for each unit of area.
The energy a particle has because it is moving.

items: Raise the temperature at constant pressure: the volume **increases**.
Lower the temperature at constant pressure: the volume **decreases**.
Raise the pressure at constant temperature: the volume **decreases**.
Lower the pressure at constant temperature: the volume **increases**.
The particles of a gas are far apart and move randomly at high speed.
Pressure is caused by the particles colliding with the walls.
Heating gives the particles more kinetic energy, so they move faster.
Faster particles hit the walls more often and with more force.
If the gas can expand, it does, until the collisions are back to the same pressure. The volume increases.
Squeezing a gas into a smaller volume makes the particles hit the walls more often. The pressure increases.
Lowering the pressure gives the particles more room, so they are further apart.

items: Higher temperature makes a gas expand. Higher pressure makes it shrink.
Gas pressure is caused by particles hitting the walls.
Hotter particles move faster, so they collide harder and more often.

blocks.text: Diffusion happens in gases and liquids. This section covers what it is and why it happens.

items.meaning: The net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration, until they are evenly spread.
The sum of the relative atomic masses of all the atoms in a molecule.

items: Particles in gases and liquids move randomly all the time.
They spread out in all directions, so they move away from where they are crowded.
More particles move from the high concentration than back to it, so there is a net movement down the concentration gradient.
Diffusion stops when the particles are evenly spread. They keep moving.
Diffusion needs no energy from outside and no stirring.
It cannot happen in solids, because the particles only vibrate in fixed positions.
A coloured crystal in water slowly spreads its colour through the water. The particles spread out, so the colour becomes paler as the solution is diluted.
The smell of cooking spreads through a room.

Ammonia and hydrogen chloride gases are released at opposite ends of a long tube. A white ring of ammonium chloride forms nearer the hydrogen chloride end. Ammonia has the lower Mr, so it diffuses faster and travels further.
Diffusion is the net movement of particles from high to low concentration.
It is caused by the random movement of particles.
It happens in gases and liquids, not in solids.

sections.heading: (Supplement) Mass and the rate of diffusion

blocks.text: (Supplement) Not all gases diffuse at the same rate. This section covers how the relative molecular mass affects it.

items: At the same temperature, particles of a gas with a **lower** relative molecular mass move faster.
So a gas with a lower Mr diffuses **faster**.
A gas with a higher Mr diffuses more slowly.
To compare two gases, work out the Mr of each from the Ar values you are given.
The gas with the lower Mr diffuses faster.
Lower Mr means faster diffusion.
Higher Mr means slower diffusion.
Compare gases by working out their Mr.

checks.q: State what happens to the volume of a gas when its temperature is increased at constant pressure.
Describe how diffusion happens in a liquid.
checks.a: Particles move randomly. There is a net movement from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration until they are evenly spread.

checks.q: (Supplement) Ammonia (Mr 17) and hydrogen chloride (Mr 36.5) are released at the same time. Which diffuses faster? Explain.
checks.a: Ammonia. It has the lower relative molecular mass, so its particles move faster.

worked_example.question: Butane and but-1-ene are colourless gases at room temperature and pressure. Suggest why but-1-ene diffuses quicker than butane.
answer_points: But-1-ene has a lower relative molecular mass.
worked_example.tip: Say 'lower relative molecular mass'. Do not say 'lighter' alone.

worked_example.question: Sulfur dioxide (SO₂) and hydrogen sulfide (H₂S) are both gases. Deduce a relationship between the relative formula mass (Mr) of a gas and the speed at which a gas diffuses. Use the Ar values to help you. [Ar values: H = 1, S = 32, O = 16]
answer_points: The higher the Mr, the slower the gas diffuses.
worked_example.tip: Work out both values, then state the relationship. The reverse argument is also accepted.
